# Convergence Zone playlists

## What each directory is

| Path | Kind | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `sources/` | Raw upstream material — Spinitron exports, MichaelG's workbooks, OneNote exports, convergencezone.fm set lists | **Read-only.** Add a new export; never edit one in place. |
| `cache/` | Canonical datastore built by `tools/python/czcache/` | **Derived.** Never hand-edit. Change a source or an override and rebuild. |
| `analysis/` | Reconciliation worksheets | Regenerated by `czcache/build_missing_spins.py` and `enrich_missing_spins.py`. |
| `publication-links.json` | WordPress post identity and optional Mixcloud URL, keyed by air date | Written from real REST responses only. |
| `schema.ts` / `schema-rationale.md` | The cache schema and why each field exists | Change the schema and the rationale together. |

## The schema

`schema.ts` is the contract. Read `schema-rationale.md` before proposing a field change —
most fields exist because a specific ambiguity in the sources made them necessary.

Two things that are easy to get wrong, both documented in `czcache/README.md`:

- **`dj_ids` is not host attribution.** Two Spinitron personas display the identical name
  "Jim Causey". Hosts come from workbook presence and `overrides/participants.yaml`.
- **Repeat detection runs before classification**, so a repeat of a MichaelG episode keeps
  its class A attribution even with no workbook of its own.

## Descriptions

Three states, and only one of them reaches the site:

- `proposed` — extracted from OneNote prose by the build, **not** reviewed
- `approved` — a person signed off in `czcache/overrides/descriptions.yaml`
- `null` — no description

Never promote `proposed` to `approved`. Never write description text into the cache
directly.

## Publication

Follow `shows/convergence-zone/docs/playlist-publishing-plan.md`. Playlists are ordinary
WordPress posts in the existing **Show Playlists** category — no custom post type, no
child theme. Preserve existing post URLs, slugs, categories, and status; a missing
Mixcloud recording is normal and does not block publishing.
